g.text: Quantum tensor and rotation coefficients
Full bimodule actions · actual coefficients · fixed gradings
The balanced tensor uses both actions
Lₓ − Rₓ = ħDₓ
P(V) ⊗U P(W) ≃ P(V ⊗ W)
↦ ux ⊗ v ⊗ w − ħu ⊗ xv ⊗ w
A torus detects the quantum shift
On Pₘ: Lₓ = x; Rₓ = x − mħ
a ⊗ b ↦ a(x,ħ) b(x − mħ,ħ)
The two unit actions differ by mħ.
A braiding with these unit constraints is impossible.
Actual rotation mapping modules
Mη = Ext* [L⁺G ⋊ ℂ×] (ICλ, ICμ)
η: Mᵃ⁻² ↪ Mᵃ; Mη / ηMη ≃ E
Mη is free over k[η]; η = c₁(O(1)).
M,N bounded below; f: M → N is graded.
f mod η invertible and η injective on N imply f invertible.
The formal ħ and geometric η require a coefficient identification.
Theorems C.82.2–C.82.5; Lemma C.82.6; Exercises C.82.7.
Free reading: Bezrukavnikov–Finkelberg, arXiv:0707.3799v4.
